'''William Hugh Woodin''' (born April 23, 1955) is an American mathematician at [[Harvard University]] specializing in [[set theory]]. He has made many notable contributions to the theory of [[inner model]]s and [[determinacy]]. A type of [[large cardinal|large cardinals]], the [[Woodin cardinal|Woodin cardinals]], bears his name. In 2023, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502194908/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 2, 2023 |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members |work=National Academy of Sciences |date=May 2, 2023}}</ref>

==Biography==
William Hugh Woodin was born on April 23, 1955, in [[Tucson]], [[Arizona]] to Ann (nee Snow) and William Woodin III, the grandson of [[United States Secretary of the Treasury]] [[William Hartman Woodin]]. Hugh's father was the executive director of the Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://azheritage.org/2018/05/06/desert-museum-pioneer-bill-woodin-leaves-lasting-legacy/ |title=Desert Museum Pioneer Bill Woodin Leaves Lasting Legacy |date=May 6, 2018 |work=Arizona Heritage Alliance}}</ref>

Woodin earned a BS from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1977 followed by a [[Ph.D.]] from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1984 under [[Robert M. Solovay]]. His dissertation title was ''Discontinuous Homomorphisms of C(Ω) and Set Theory''.<ref>{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/5d39da07418bded426b2cd1e5190e65e/ |title=Discontinuous Homomorphisms of C(Ω) and Set Theory |first=W. Hugh |last=Woodin |year=1984 |institution=University of California, Berkeley |degree=PhD |oclc=892820502 |id={{Proquest|5d39da07418bded426b2cd1e5190e65e}}}}</ref>


In 1985, Woodin joined the Caltech faculty as a full professor<ref>{{cite book |url=https://campuspubs.library.caltech.edu/114/ |title=Caltech Catalog 1985-1986 |publisher=California Institute of Technology |year=1985 |page=286}}</ref> and remained there until 1988<ref>{{cite book |url=https://campuspubs.library.caltech.edu/116/ |title=Caltech Catalog 1987-1988 |publisher=California Institute of Technology |year=1987 |page=281}}</ref> when he left for UC Berkeley.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/w-hugh-woodin |title=W. Hugh Woodin |work=UC Berkeley Department of Mathematics}}</ref>

He served as [[chairman|chair]] of the Berkeley mathematics department for the 2002–2003 academic year. Woodin is a managing editor of the ''[[Journal of Mathematical Logic]]''. In 2015, Woodin retires from Berkeley<ref>{{cite web |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/bulk_7/Newsletter2015.pdf |title=Farewells and Welcomes |work=MATHEMATICS + BERKELEY |publisher=Department of Mathematics at the University of California, Berkele |date=Fall 2015 |page=7 |quote=Professor Hugh Woodin retired in January 2015.}}</ref> and moves to Harvard.

He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2000.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter W|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterW.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=June 3, 2011}}</ref>

He is the great-grandson of [[William Hartman Woodin]], former [[United States Secretary of the Treasury|Secretary of the Treasury]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}}

==Work==
Woodin's earliest mathematical work concerned a connection between set theory and the theory of [[Banach algebra|Banach algebras]].  In the 1980s he made major contributions in the study of the [[Axiom of determinacy|Axiom of Determinacy]] (AD) via [[inner model theory]], culminating in determining the
precise [[Equiconsistency#Consistency strength|consistency strength]] of AD relative to the standard [[large cardinal]] hierarchy.<ref name="KanTHI">{{cite book |last1=Kanamori |first1=Akihiro |title=The Higher Infinite |date=2003 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin |pages=450–471 |edition=2nd}}</ref>  

Woodin has done work on the theory of generic multiverses and the related concept of [[Ω-logic]], which suggested an argument that the [[continuum hypothesis]] is either undecidable or false in the sense of [[mathematical platonism]]. Woodin criticizes this view arguing that it leads to a counterintuitive reduction in which all truths in the set theoretical universe can be decided from a small part of it. He claims that these and related mathematical results lead (intuitively) to the conclusion that the continuum hypothesis has a [[truth value]] and the Platonistic approach is reasonable.

Woodin now predicts that there should be a way of constructing an inner model for almost all known large cardinals, which he calls the Ultimate L and which would have similar properties as [[Constructible universe|Gödel's constructible universe]]. In particular, the continuum hypothesis would be true in this universe.<ref name="Quanta Magazine 2013 h695">{{cite web |last=Wolchover |first=Natalie| title=To Settle Infinity Dispute, a New Law of Logic | website=Quanta Magazine | date=2013-11-26 | url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/to-settle-infinity-question-a-new-law-of-mathematics-20131126/ | access-date=2024-03-23}}</ref>

== Honors ==
In 2008, Woodin gave the [[Gödel Lecture]] titled ''The Continuum Hypothesis, the Conjecture, and the inner model problem of one supercompact cardinal.'' 
In 2010, he was a plenary speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/ICM2010/offline/www.icm2010.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers.html |title=ICM 2010 Invited Speakers page |year=2010 |work=[[International Mathematical Union]]}}</ref>
In 2018, he was the [[Tarski Lectures|Tarski lecturer]].
